statement: For distinct real osculation points and zero-dimensional Grassmannian Schubert conditions, the intersection is transverse and consists of the expected number of distinct real points.

answer.text: For distinct real osculation points and zero-dimensional Grassmannian Schubert conditions, the intersection is transverse and consists of the expected number of distinct real points.
answer.display: No exceptional fibre on the distinct-real osculation locus

notes:
The conclusion applies to the distinct-real osculation locus; it does not describe the entire complex discriminant. Strong transversality is attributed to this Corollary, not to the original Shapiro theorem or Levinson–Purbhoo. Migration: Merge exceptional-fibre behaviour into Exceptional locus; preserve each source result separately.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_4f176aaecb906e01; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

Consequently this distinct-real-parameter locus contains no nonreduced or positive-dimensional fibre.
scope: Zero-dimensional Grassmannian Schubert problems restricted to flags osculating one rational normal curve; real lower bounds allow conjugate pairs, total reality/transversality requires distinct real osculation points.
